subject: Request: One-time pricing flex for BrightHealth due to prefetch roadmap delay
messages:
From: Beth Wolfe <beth.wolfe@brighthealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Impact from prefetch delay — request for temporary pricing support

Hi Hannah,

Quick update from our side: the prefetch feature you flagged in the roadmap hit a hard dependency at our side and the BrightHealth dev schedule slipped by ~9 weeks. That means our planned production launch that would have driven projected usage for Q3 is late.

Procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a short-term pricing accommodation (one-off credit or temporary rate) to help bridge the launch gap while we finalize the integration. This is time sensitive for our CFO and procurement team — they want to get a commercial hold in place this week before our budget review.

Attached is a one-page impact summary (usage lost by month). Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Beth
Beth Wolfe
Director, Platform Partnerships
BrightHealth

Attachment: brighthealth_impact_summary.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Wolfe <beth.wolfe@brighthealth.com>
Cc: procurement@brighthealth.com
Date: 2027-05-16T10:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Impact from prefetch delay — request for temporary pricing support

Hi Beth — thanks for the context and the summary. Sorry to hear about the slip.

We can consider a limited commercial accommodation tied to the roadmap timing rather than a blanket credit. High level proposal: a time-boxed 20% rate reduction on generated tokens for the first 3 months after their production launch (or a one-time credit equivalent to 3 months of forecast usage, whichever is greater), with an agreed mutual action plan that documents the expected launch date and integration checkpoints.

I need to escalate for exec approval and finance gating — I’ll loop in the pricing/finance leads and legal for the DocuSign wording. Can you confirm the updated expected launch week (best guess) and whether the CFO needs the accommodation captured on a PO or via DocuSign?

I’ll follow up shortly with internal ask and a concrete authorization request.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: k.i@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-16T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightHealth — pricing accommodation request (exec approval needed)

Team — forwarding BrightHealth request. TL;DR: prefetch roadmap delay pushed BrightHealth launch ~9 weeks; they’re asking for a short-term pricing accommodation to preserve the launch. Attached impact summary from the customer.

Ask: I’m requesting approval for a conditional, time-boxed commercial override: 20% off generation tokens for first 3 months post-launch OR a one-time credit equal to 3 months forecast (whichever is greater). Restrictions: limited to this specific launch, documented MAP, non-precedent setting language, and a firm production launch checkpoint.

Why: this is a $1.2M ARR+ opportunity this year, retention and expansion likely if we keep them on track. The customer's procurement needs something in writing this week.

What I need from each of you:
- Karthik: legal language + whether we can do DocuSign amendment as a temporary concession vs an SOW.
- Laura: finance — confirm the accounting treatment and max credit we can approve at AM level vs. FP&A signoff.
- Marcus: product — quick confirmation of roadmap ETA and whether there’s any technical quick fix (prefetch shim) we can offer to shorten the delay.
- Marissa: CS — operational guardrails for monitoring usage and rollback triggers.

If you can reply by EOD today, I’ll craft the final approval note for exec sign-off.

Thanks,
Hannah

Attachment: redwood_prefetch_roadmap_snip.png
From: k.i@redwood.ai <k.i@redwood.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-16T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightHealth — pricing accommodation request (exec approval needed)

Hannah — thanks for the summary. From legal perspective we can support a time-limited commercial amendment via DocuSign but need: (1) explicit termination clause for the concession, (2) non-precedent language, and (3) clear acceptance criteria tied to the mutually agreed launch week. I’ll draft a short amendment template.

Also please include expected ARR impact and the exact credit cap (not just percent) so finance can run scenarios.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, k.i@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-17T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightHealth — pricing accommodation request (exec approval needed)

Have looked at numbers. We can approve up to a $45k one-time credit at AM level; anything above requires FP&A sign-off (1–2 business days). If Hannah proposes the 20% for 3 months, please send forecasted token volumes so I can model the cap.

Accounting note: categorize as commercial discount; need to record the concession and include an expiration date in the amendment. Also suggest a monthly usage cadence check so we can claw back if usage deviates materially from forecast.

I’ll standby to review the wording once Karthik drafts.

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Wolfe <beth.wolfe@brighthealth.com>
Cc: procurement@brighthealth.com, k.i@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-20T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Impact from prefetch delay — request for temporary pricing support

Beth — thank you for the patience while we reviewed internally. Good news: we can offer a conditional commercial accommodation. Summary below: 

- Offer: 20% rate reduction on generation tokens for the first 3 full months after BrightHealth’s production launch (documented launch week in amendment) OR a one-time credit capped at $45,000 if forecast volume makes the percent option exceed that cap.
- Conditions: (1) Mutual action plan signed and attached to the amendment; (2) Concession expires automatically if BrightHealth does not enter production within 16 weeks of the amendment signing; (3) Monthly usage reviews with CS (Marissa) for variance checks and rollback triggers.
- Next steps: I’ll send a short DocuSign amendment (Karthik is preparing language). Please confirm: (a) final expected production week (best estimate), and (b) whether the procurement team prefers a PO + amendment or DocuSign alone.

Attached: draft concession terms (for internal review) and DocuSign packet will follow.

If that works, I’ll route for rapid exec sign-off and send DocuSign later today.

Best,
Hannah
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: docusign_pricing_vers1.pdf
